alternatives.reason: A summary written by the renderer (or by a model) would add facts the DecisionRecord does not hold. The plain-language summary is a human-supplied request field (owner_summary); when it is missing the Change is NEEDS_INPUT with the requester as owner.

Rewriting accepted decisions would change what was decided. Older decisions render with an explicit 'no plain-language summary' notice and the technical objective shown unedited; a summary arrives only through a new request version.

The renderer emits structured values (change-decision-brief/v2); the workspace owns headings and labels through the existing t() dictionary, so the Brief follows the locale without a server catalogue. Data values are never translated.

Receipt conclusion-first layout and a reviewer-facing Technical Report (review items 4–5) are separate slices; the role-reader test (item 6) is the acceptance evidence for readability and is still open.

architecture_impact: Request and DecisionRecord gain owner_summary; evaluate() reports owner_summary missing (owner: requester) so a Change cannot be decided without it; the decision copies it verbatim.

RenderBrief(decision, staleness) returns change-decision-brief/v2: state (ACCEPTED/STALE + stale_reason), owner_summary / owner_summary_missing, objective, selected option (id, title, summary) resolved from the recorded alternatives, route (source, target, transition, target_ref, production_action), risk_level, unknowns, in_scope, out_of_scope, required_evidence (sorted), decided_by, remaining alternatives, lineage. Headline and prose sections are removed; the renderer only selects and orders recorded values.

frontend/src/components/ChangeBrief.tsx renders the Brief in reader-question order — summary, route, accepted risk (warning when unknowns exist), scope, next gate, who decided, alternatives — with ids, hashes, transition and policy in a collapsed traceability block; headings, evidence-code labels and risk labels go through t(), data values do not.
Agent Context Pack is unchanged; Brief and Pack keep identical lineage.

Evaluation and DecisionRecord record promotion_path: the active environments of the bound topology version in sequence order. The Brief route carries it and the workspace draws it, marking where the approval ends; decisions without a recorded path show only source and target with a note.

RuleAdvisor sentences come from one coded table (advisor.go ruleNotes / ruleOptionIDs). The Brief sends unknowns as {text, code, value} and rule options with a code; frontend/src/i18n/advisor.ts shows coded wording in zh-TW. Human or model text has no code and is shown as recorded; the English text remains the recorded value.
cost_assumptions: No cloud resources; backend render + frontend only.
unknowns: Readability is asserted by structure and screenshots only; no role reader has answered the three questions yet (G5).
Evidence-code labels cover the codes the current topologies declare; unknown codes render as the code itself.
The EB-012 CHG-001 decision predates owner_summary and renders with the missing-summary notice.
Other server-generated text (missing-input reasons, observations, gate details) is still English in zh-TW; only rule-advisor options and unknowns are coded.
acceptance_criteria: A Change without owner_summary is NEEDS_INPUT with owner_summary owned by the requester.
The Brief leads with the owner summary verbatim; option ids, hashes and policy appear only in the traceability block and the lineage strip.
The selected option is shown by title and is not repeated among the alternatives; production_action forbidden is stated in plain words.
A decision without owner_summary says so and shows the technical objective unedited instead of substituting text.
Switching to zh-TW translates Brief headings and labels; summary, objective, scope lines, unknowns and rationale read back unchanged.
Brief and Agent Context Pack lineage stay identical; STALE still shows with its reason.
The Brief shows the recorded promotion path and marks the target as the end of the approval; later environments read as needing another decision, production as not authorized.
In zh-TW, rule-advisor options and unknowns read in Chinese; owner summary, rationale and any uncoded text read back unchanged.

Follow-ups asked by the owner on the same branch: a flow diagram for the route ("可以 你先做看看") and removing English system text from the zh-TW Brief ("可以").
